issue.body:
Fixes #11440, fixes #11546

### Description of change

When using upsert or orUpdate query with `schema name` and `skipUpdateIfNoValuesChanged` in entity produces wrong SQL that throws an error

Expected Behavior
`..."schemaName"."tableName"."name"  IS DISTINCT FROM...` should be generated

Actual Behavior
`..."schemaName.tableName"."name"  IS DISTINCT FROM...` actually generated

This fix addresses a regression introduced in pull request #11082 by ensuring correct handling of alias names and table names when they are equal or distinct when entities use schema. When alias name does not match with main table name the escaped alias is used or else the table name is used in a proper format.

issue.title: Issue with upsert Method and skipUpdateIfNoValuesChanged

repository.name: typeorm
repository.description: ORM for TypeScript and JavaScript. Supports MySQL, PostgreSQL, MariaDB, SQLite, MS SQL Server, Oracle, SAP Hana, WebSQL databases. Works in NodeJS, Browser, Ionic, Cordova and Electron platforms.

issue.body:
### Issue description

When using the upsert method with skipUpdateIfNoValuesChanged, the query uses the correct "schemaName"."tableName" format initially but switches to "schemaName.tableName" after the WHERE clause, causing the query to fail. Expected Behavior

### Expected Behavior

The upsert method should generate a query that consistently uses the correct schema and table name format throughout the query. For example:
```sql
INSERT INTO "schema"."table" ("id", "name")
VALUES ($1, $2)
ON CONFLICT ("id") DO UPDATE
SET "name" = EXCLUDED."name"
WHERE "schema"."table"."name" IS DISTINCT FROM EXCLUDED."name";
```

### Actual Behavior

The query generated by the upsert method starts with the correct schema and table name format but switches to an incorrect format after the WHERE clause. For example:
```sql
INSERT INTO "schema"."table" ("id", "name")
VALUES ($1, $2)
ON CONFLICT ("id") DO UPDATE
SET "name" = EXCLUDED."name"
WHERE "schema.table"."name" IS DISTINCT FROM EXCLUDED."name";
```

### Steps to reproduce

Create a simple entity:
```ts
@Entity({ schema: "test", name: "example" })
export class Example {
    @PrimaryGeneratedColumn()
    id: number;

    @Column()
    name: string;
}
```
Use the upsert method:
```ts
const example = new Example () as DeepPartial<Example>;

await repository.upsert(example, {
    conflictPaths: {"id": true},
     skipUpdateIfNoValuesChanged: true
});
```

### My Environment

| Dependency          | Version  |
| ---                 | ---      |
| Operating System   | Windows|
| Node.js  | 20.12.2|
| Typescript   | 5.8.3 |
| TypeORM    | 0.3.24 |
| NestJS     | 11.1.1|
